fields.end_condition: Ongoing statutory large-load standards; no sunset in the enacted bill text.

evidence.title: Texas SB 6, enrolled text
evidence.supports: Enacted text establishes ERCOT large-load interconnection, cost, disclosure, financial commitment, and emergency-curtailment requirements, with a default 75 MW threshold.
evidence.quote: The commission shall establish a demand threshold of 75 megawatts unless the commission determines that a lower threshold is necessary.

decisions.notes: SB 6 is a binding utility/grid restriction, not a development-permitting moratorium.

new_bills.bill: Governor Abbott August 3, 2026 Data Center Audit Directive
new_bills.status: Governor directive issued 2026-08-03; ERCOT implementation notice issued 2026-08-03.
new_bills.end_condition: Until PUCT and ERCOT complete the comprehensive verification and audit; projects that fail applicable requirements must be denied grid connection.
new_bills.key_provisions: Directs PUCT and ERCOT to verify and audit every data center advancing through ERCOT interconnection before it may move forward, pausing the Batch Zero process pending the required review.

evidence.title: Governor Abbott Directs Comprehensive Data Center Audit
evidence.supports: Governor's official release directs PUCT and ERCOT to complete the audit before any data-center project moves forward and requires denial of noncompliant grid connections.

evidence.title: ERCOT Market Notice M-A080326-01
evidence.supports: ERCOT says it received the Governor's letter and will not advance the Batch Zero interconnection-study notifications on the scheduled timeline.

new_bills.notes: This is an in-force utility-grid restriction on ERCOT interconnection progress, not a statewide land-use or permitting moratorium.
